✳ nightwatch.

Made for the moments between sunset and sunrise.

Weather: Open-Meteo · Astronomy: SunCalc

Reading the sky

The viewing score is a planning estimate, not a measurement of atmospheric seeing. It combines cloud cover (60%), humidity (15%), wind (10%), and moonlight above the horizon (15%). Twilight reduces the score; daylight scores zero.

Astronomical darkness means the Sun is at least 18° below the horizon. Sun and Moon positions and illumination are calculated with SunCalc. The best window is the highest-scoring consecutive block of up to three dark hours.

Local light pollution, smoke, transparency, and upper-atmosphere turbulence are not modeled. Forecasts can change. Times use the selected location’s time zone.
